transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-19
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Lin (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Sofia Ruiz (Redwood CSM), Laura Chen (HearthBank - Procurement), Miguel Santos (HearthBank - Security), Priya Rao (HearthBank - Legal), Evan Brooks (HearthBank - CTO)

Summary (auto):
HearthBank is moving forward with Redwood for inference - primary ask is review of MSA/DPA, confirmation of SLAs, and approval of pricing for Dedicated/reserved capacity vs hosted. Security team requested KMS and audit log details, legal has a few redlines on data residency and indemnity. Next step is Redwood to send updated MSA/DPA with SSO clause and Dedicated pricing spreadsheet; schedule technical benchmark for private deployment.

Topics: MSA items, DPA / data residency, SLAs and uptime targets, pricing (hosted vs dedicated), onboarding runbook, security documentation (SOC2, pen test, KMS), timeline for procurement approvals.

Action items (captured): see metadata.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie (Redwood AE): Okay hi everyone, thanks for joining—this is Jamie from Redwood, with Marcus on the SE side and Sofia our customer success. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Laura (HearthBank): Good, thanks. We've got a pretty packed agenda, procurement wants to make sure we can sign MSA and DPA and the security team has some questions.
[00:12] Jamie: Totally, that's what we want to cover. We'll walk through the standard MSA/DPA items, call out anything special for fintech, then go through SLAs and pricing options — hosted API versus Dedicated reserved pools or Private/VPC — and then agree next steps.
[00:25] Evan (CTO): Quick ask up front, we need to understand data residency and KMS integration. We can't have any customer PII leaving our EU region without encryption and KMS control.
[00:33] Marcus (Redwood SE): Yep, we can support customer-managed keys; Redwood Private supports bring-your-own KMS and HSM integrations. For hosted we have customer-segregated projects but for strict key control we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[00:44] Miguel (Security): When you say "customer-managed keys" — is the key material never in Redwood's control? We need to know about key rotation and audit logs.
[00:51] Marcus: Correct, in Private/VPC or dedicated setups the keys are in your KMS (e.g., AWS KMS or external HSM) and Redwood never has plaintext key material. Rotation is supported via standard KMS APIs, and we can ship audit logs for all KMS calls and access events. I'll share the specific audit schema after this call.
[01:05] Priya (Legal): On the MSA, we have two primary redlines: data residency guarantees to keep EU customer data in EU region, and a limitation/modification to the indemnity clause. Also, we need to make sure the DPA covers subprocessors.
[01:17] Jamie: Totally understood — our typical MSA includes region pinning clauses for Dedicated/Private and the DPA lists subprocessors; we can accept a reasonable redline on indemnity. We'll send a version with the SSO/SAML and data residency language included.
[01:29] Laura: Timeline-wise, procurement hopes to finish approvals in two weeks if legal signoff is straightforward. Is that feasible?
[01:34] Jamie: Yes, that's reasonable. We'll aim to get the updated MSA/DPA to you in 3 business days, so you have time to review.
[01:39] [short cross-talk] Sofia (CSM): I'll add onboarding checklist and the standard security pack — SOC 2 Type II, penetration test summary, and architecture diagram.
[01:48] Miguel: That would be helpful. We also want to see network diagrams for the VPC/private control plane.
[01:53] Marcus: We'll include the VPC flow and private control plane architecture. Also worth noting: our runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching to reduce cost, but I might say that poorly earlier — sometimes the transcript says "K-V cash".
[02:05] Evan: Ha, understood. On SLAs, what uptime and latency SLOs do you offer for Dedicated vs hosted? Our app needs predictable 95th percentile latency under load.
[02:13] Jamie: For hosted we typically advertise best-effort with published median latencies — it's optimized for quick time-to-value. Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime of 99.95% and latency SLOs tuned per reserved pool; we can commit to 95th percentile targets per model profile in the contract. Marcus can chime in on the numbers.
[02:28] Marcus: For the example config we ran with a 4-GPU Dedicated pool we saw 95th percentile generation latencies around 250–400ms for chat-style 1k token contexts on a 13B model, with continuous batching. If you need stricter latency we can recommend a different instance mix or autoscaling.
[02:45] Miguel: Are there fallbacks if a region loses capacity? We need graceful degradation and audit trails.
[02:51] Marcus: Yes, smart routing supports automated fallback to another region or to a different model variant; that behavior can be encoded in routing policies. All failover events and request traces are in the audit logs.
[03:03] Priya: On pricing — we received the hosted per-token sheet and it's fine for low volume, but procurement wants to compare Dedicated reserved monthly commits. Can you walk through the pricing again?
[03:12] Jamie: Sure — quick high level: hosted is usage-based per-token and per-embedding. Dedicated is a monthly commit for GPU pools; you pay reserved monthly for capacity and get predictable unit costs and isolation. We have burst credits for short spikes. Marcus, example costs?
[03:24] Marcus: Example: a 4xA100-equivalent Dedicated pool is $X/month (we'll provide a spreadsheet), which maps to about Y tokens/sec sustained. Generally Dedicated reduces per-token cost by 30–50% for high-volume workloads compared to hosted. Exact numbers depend on batching, quantization profile, and sequence lengths.
[03:42] Evan: We expect ramp to tens of millions of tokens per month within Q1. That profile favors Dedicated. Procurement needs the exact mapping so finance can approve.
[03:50] Jamie: We'll send the Dedicated pricing spreadsheet with several configurations and a calculator to estimate monthly cost given tokens/second and average context length.
[03:57] Laura: For contracting, procurement also wants the SLA credits table and termination for convenience terms — can those be added?
[04:03] Jamie: SLA credits are included in Dedicated contracts. Termination for convenience is negotiable within reason — we'll provide standard language and you can propose edits.
[04:10] Priya: We will propose a modest change to the termination clause and provide our recommended language. Also looking at the DPA, we flagged subprocessors and want the option to be notified 30 days before onboarding a new subprocessor.
[04:21] Jamie: That's acceptable; our standard DPA has notification windows and subprocessors listed. We'll add the 30-day notice clause in the version we send.
[04:28] Miguel: Regarding encryption at rest and in transit, can you confirm FIPS endpoints for KMS calls? We need FIPS 140-2 compliance for certain workloads.
[04:36] Marcus: We can route KMS calls through your FIPS-enabled KMS if needed. On the service side we support TLS 1.2/1.3 and encryption at rest using customer-managed keys for Private deployments. I'll include the specifics in the security pack.
[04:48] Evan: One more operational question: what's the onboarding timeline for Dedicated vs Private? We're concerned about procurement lead time and engineering window.
[04:56] Sofia: Typical Dedicated onboarding is 2–4 weeks — that includes capacity provisioning, model pinning, and route setup. Private/VPC can be 4–8 weeks depending on network approvals and air-gap needs.
[05:07] Laura: That's fine as long as procurement and legal can finish in two weeks. We want to have the contract in place so engineering can start provisioning in early December.
[05:15] Jamie: Sounds good — target contract signature by end of November to hit early December provisioning.
[05:19] [silence / typing]
[05:25] Priya: A few legal items: we request a mutual limitation of liability up to fees paid in the preceding 12 months, and clarification of data ownership — that customer retains ownership and Redwood is a processor.
[05:36] Jamie: Understood — our baseline is mutual liability with some carveouts. We'll put together suggested language aligning with your ask.
[05:41] Miguel: Also, will Redwood accept a security questionnaire? Our vendor security team uses a standard 300+ question RFP.
[05:48] Sofia: Yes, we can respond to the security questionnaire — we also have a short vendor pack with SOC2, architecture, pen test summary that usually answers most items. If there are remaining gaps we can coordinate follow-ups.
[05:59] Evan: For the benchmark — can Redwood run a private benchmark in our environment or do you need us to run it? We prefer Redwood-run with our dataset in a staging VPC for reproducible numbers.
[06:09] Marcus: We support both. For Private/VPC deployments we typically run the benchmark together: we provide the runbook and remote assistance, and we can run tests inside your staging VPC with your dataset. We'll need S3 access or a signed dataset and an allowed IP range.
[06:22] Laura: We'll coordinate S3 access. Procurement also needs to know about insurance and SOC2 certs for the contract.
[06:29] Jamie: We'll include our insurance certificate and SOC2 Type II report in the pack.
[06:33] [short pause]
[06:38] Priya: One more: indemnity around data breaches — we want clarity on notification windows and responsibility for breach costs.
[06:45] Jamie: Standard is notification within 72 hours of becoming aware, cooperation on remediation, and liabilities tied to negligence — we'll provide the typical MSA section and we can discuss specific carveouts.
[06:56] Miguel: Will you sign on to a clause requiring periodic pen testing by HearthBank? We may want the option to commission a pen test with Redwood's coordination.
[07:04] Marcus: That's fine — we do annual internal pen testing and can coordinate third-party tests; typically we require scope agreement and safe-guarding procedures.
[07:13] Evan: OK, this is all great. Do you have any examples of finance-friendly clauses for committed spend? We want to avoid large termination penalties.
[07:22] Jamie: We can provide a committed spend schedule with phased reductions and a fair termination schedule — that's usually how we work with mid-market finance teams.
[07:30] Laura: Great. Any other blockers from Redwood?
[07:34] Jamie: Just to confirm we'll send the updated MSA/DPA with the requested SSO/KMS/data residency language, the Dedicated pricing spreadsheet, security pack, and the benchmark runbook. We'll also set up the benchmark week of Nov 30 as a placeholder.
[07:49] Priya: We'll aim to send redlines within two business days of receiving your drafts.
[07:53] Sofia: I'll set the calendar invite for the week of Nov 30 and include the runbook.
[08:00] [wrap up summary] Jamie: Quick recap — Redwood action: MSA/DPA drafts with SSO/KMS/30-day subprocessor notice, Dedicated pricing spreadsheet + calculator, security pack (SOC2, pen test summary, architecture), benchmark runbook. HearthBank action: legal redlines, provide test dataset and S3 access, procurement to review pricing. Target: contract execution by end of November.
[08:22] Evan: That aligns with our internal plan. Thanks everyone.
[08:26] Jamie: Thanks all — we'll follow up via email with artifacts.

End of transcript.

Attachments referenced: Dedicated-pricing.xlsx (link in follow-up email), Redwood-Security-Pack.pdf (SOC2, pen test summary, architecture), Redwood-MSA-DPA-draft.docx (sent after call), Benchmark-runbook.md (link).

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-recognition (e.g., "K-V cash" instead of KV cache), speaker tags approximate.
